text_blocks.snippet: Several medications can lead to low sodium levels (hyponatremia), including diuretics, antidepressants, and certain anticonvulsants. Specifically, thiazide diuretics like hydrochlorothiazide and chlortalidone, and loop diuretics like furosemide, are known to increase the risk of hyponatremia. Additionally, some antidepressants, particularly SSRIs like sertraline and fluoxetine, and anticonvulsants like carbamazepine, can also cause hyponatremia.

list.title: Thiazide diuretics:
list.snippet: These are commonly used for high blood pressure and heart failure. They work by increasing sodium and water excretion through the kidneys.

list.title: Loop diuretics:
list.snippet: Also used for heart failure, these medications also promote sodium and water loss.

list.title: SSRIs (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors):
list.snippet: These antidepressants, including sertraline and fluoxetine, can sometimes lead to hyponatremia, particularly in older adults.

list.title: Other antidepressants:
list.snippet: Some other antidepressants like tricyclic antidepressants and SNRIs (Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors) have also been associated with hyponatremia.

list.title: Carbamazepine:
list.snippet: This medication, used to treat seizures, has a notable association with drug-induced hyponatremia.

list.title: Oxcarbazepine:
list.snippet: Similar to carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine is also associated with a higher risk of hyponatremia.
ACE inhibitors and ARBs: These medications for high blood pressure can also contribute to hyponatremia in some cases.
Proton pump inhibitors: Some studies have shown an association between PPIs and hyponatremia.
Antipsychotics: Certain antipsychotic medications can also cause low sodium levels.
Hyponatremia can be asymptomatic or cause symptoms like nausea, headache, confusion, and in severe cases, seizures.
The risk of hyponatremia can be higher in older adults, those with certain medical conditions (like heart failure or kidney disease), and those taking multiple medications that can lower sodium.
If you are concerned about hyponatremia or experiencing symptoms, it's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and management.
